infra-context · generated

Infra map: Bunkai TMS

Generated 2026-11-13 from upex-bunkai-tms at origin/staging 63d5e7e3, live staging (read-only role), the business data, API and E2E maps of the same date, and the August 2026 legacy markdown as input.

Overview

Bunkai is a Next.js 15 App Router full-stack monolith on Vercel, backed by Supabase. Pages (React Server Components) and the REST API (app/api/v1/**/route.ts, 113 route files) live in the same app: there is no separate API tier. Every API handler goes through withApiHandler() (lib/api/handler.ts). There is no ORM: data goes through supabase-js (PostgREST) and SECURITY DEFINER RPCs.

Deployment shape: one Vercel project serving staging and production from different deployments, plus Vercel Cron for two daily jobs; one Supabase project (Postgres, Auth, Storage, Realtime, Vault) shared by local, staging and production (.context/release/pending-production-v2.md in the target repo). Background work uses Vercel after(), Vercel Cron and pg_cron; there is no queue.

Surfaces outside the public API: two cron routes (/api/v1/admin/send-digest, /api/v1/admin/storage-cleanup, both gated by CRON_SECRET), the Stripe webhook (POST /api/v1/billing/webhook, gated by signature), and GET /api/v1/health (public).

Containers and data flow

  • Browser to app: HTTPS with the Supabase session cookie; middleware.ts refreshes it on every page request.
  • Browser to Supabase directly: signed upload PUT into the private run-evidence bucket, and Realtime subscriptions on run_atcs, run_steps, notifications, chat_messages.
  • Agent or CI to app: Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_*, optional Idempotency-Key.
  • Vercel Cron to app: send-digest daily 08:00 UTC, storage-cleanup daily 03:00 UTC, Bearer CRON_SECRET. Vercel registers crons only from the production deployment, so they never fire on staging.
  • App to Supabase Auth: password, OTP, magic link and OAuth exchanges.
  • App to Postgres: PostgREST and RPCs as the user (cookie client), as the PAT's user (per-request JWT) or with the service role (idempotency, tokens, rate limit, storage, cron, Vault).
  • App to Storage: service-role signed URLs, ranged reads, deletes.
  • App to externals: Jira Cloud REST v3 with per-workspace credentials from Vault, Stripe Checkout and invoices, Resend emails. Stripe to app: signed webhook.
  • Inside Postgres: 4 pg_cron jobs (run sweeps every 15 and every 5 minutes, deleted-workspace purge at 03:00, rate-limit cleanup hourly); data map automatic-processes.

Auth flow

Browser users (Supabase Auth, cookie session):

  1. POST /api/v1/auth/check-email (public, rate limited) tells the UI which path to show.
  2. Existing account: POST /api/v1/auth/signin runs the Supabase password grant, sets the session cookies and also returns a fresh PAT with the default scopes.
  3. New account: signup, then a mandatory 6-digit OTP through confirm (resend re-sends). Magic link: magic-link, verified at /auth/callback.
  4. OAuth (GitHub, Google): GET /auth/oauth/{provider} sets a 600 s state cookie; /auth/callback compares it in constant time and exchanges the PKCE code.
  5. Every page request: middleware.ts refreshes the session and sends anonymous users on protected prefixes to /login?next=. A separate bk_active_ws cookie remembers the active workspace (a preference, not authorization).

Agents and CI (PAT):

  1. Get a PAT from signin or confirm (scopes atc:read atc:write run:execute), or mint one with POST /api/v1/tokens from a browser session (workspace:admin only for an owner or admin).
  2. Call with Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>; the gateway looks up the prefix, compares the SHA-256 of the secret, checks expiry and revocation, and answers a uniform 401 on any failure.
  3. The gateway mints a 60-second user JWT so queries run under RLS as the token's owner, then checks the route's capability. The concrete requests are in backend.

Every route declares one posture (public, cookie-only, authenticated, required) at compile time; counts per posture: api map auth-model.

Database

One Supabase Postgres. Live staging shows 52 public tables, all under RLS, with 97 RLS policies, 129 bunkai_* functions and 23 triggers, matching the migrations (data map entities). Table groups: tenancy and access; catalog (projects, modules, stories, criteria, ATCs); tests, plans and milestones; run snapshots; bugs; billing; Jira; notifications, activity and chat; cross-cutting (idempotency, rate limits, storage cleanup, saved views, deletions and exports). Multi-table writes go through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs. Tables, columns and lifecycles: business-data-context.

Performance hooks

No caching layer: the old in-process coverage cache was removed (one workspace RPC per render, lib/home/coverage.ts). Pagination caps, size caps, timeouts and the one rate limiter are listed in nfr-performance. Idempotency replays protect creates for 24 hours (lib/api/idempotency.ts).

ADRs

The target repo keeps its own decision log in .context/ADR/ (46 files: auth model, idempotency, run snapshots, Vault credentials and more); this map cites it by number. The QA framework's own test-architecture decisions found in this discovery are recorded in this repo: .context/ADR/ADR-0026-two-auth-rails-in-tests.md, ADR-0027-data-testid-selector-contract.md, ADR-0028-serial-workspace-scoped-test-data.md.

QA relevance

  • Two auth rails to cover: the cookie session for UI and cookie-only routes, the PAT for API and agent flows. A PAT cannot mint a PAT, so admin token tests need a browser session.
  • Staging never runs the Vercel crons: time-based behaviour (digest, storage cleanup) has to be triggered with an authenticated POST, the secret referenced by name only.
  • RLS is the last line of defence: cross-workspace tests must use identities from different workspaces.
  • Realtime drives live run updates: UI tests wait on pushed changes, not on reloads.

Failures a test must account for

  • Stripe webhook: missing or bad signature answers 400 bad_request; unhandled event types answer 200 ignored; an unknown session or a customer seen in the last hour answers 5xx so Stripe redelivers; deliveries are de-duplicated in stripe_webhook_events. Without Stripe keys, checkout answers 503 payment_processor_unavailable.
  • Cron routes: no or wrong Bearer answers 401; both GET (Vercel) and POST (manual) are gated.
  • Jira: an auth failure fails the whole job, per-issue errors are listed on the job, HTTP 429 backs off 1-2-4-8-16 s; no connection answers 409 jira_not_connected; the result arrives after a 202, so poll the job.
  • Storage down answers 503 storage_unavailable; an uncommitted upload stays invisible.
  • Resend key missing: the digest fails per user and is logged; the app still boots.

Environment variables (names only)

Required: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (both inlined at build), SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, CRON_SECRET (boot fails without it).

Optional: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL (default http://localhost:3000), SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET, RESEND_DIGEST_FROM_EMAIL (default sandbox sender).

External service: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, STRIPE_CLOUD_PRICE_ID, RESEND_API_KEY, ATLASSIAN_URL (read by the app, deliberately absent from .env.example). Platform: VERCEL_ENV (maps production, preview to staging, else local), NODE_ENV.

Drift: .env.example lists SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, but the runtime reads NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY; a clone filled from .env.example fails validation at boot. .env.example also omits CRON_SECRET and the Stripe names.

Build configuration

next.config.ts holds four settings: reactStrictMode, outputFileTracingRoot, typedRoutes, images.remotePatterns: []. No standalone output, no headers, redirects or rewrites, no custom webpack.

Local development setup

The target README is the generic framework README, not an app runbook; this recipe comes from the scripts and lib/env.ts and was not executed. There is no local database: local always points at the shared Supabase project.

The /qa testability page

The target publishes a public, Spanish testability page at /qa (200 on staging and production, root data-testid="qa-page"), generated by the dev team's testability-guide skill (snapshot dated 2026-06-24). It documents DBHub access, the OpenAPI MCP, the PAT flow and the login test ids, and points credentials to a Jira epic instead of inlining them. Its auth facts agree with the code; it is not an env source for running the app (it lists QA slots only).

Code splitting, bundle and performance

SEO and browser support

Root metadata title "Bunkai — Test Management System" with metadataBase hardcoded to http://localhost:3000; no robots, sitemap, manifest or Open Graph tags (staging /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml answer 404). No browserslist: Next defaults. No i18n: <html lang="en">, and only /qa is in Spanish.

Routing, state and auth integration points

  • Routes: app/(auth)/login public; app/(app)/ protected (home, projects with ATCs, bugs, metrics, milestones, plans, runs, settings, tests, traceability; onboarding, activity, ATC library, settings, workspace members); public /, /about, /design-tokens, /qa, /api/docs, /auth/*, the restore landing. / redirects by auth state.
  • State: no state library; scoped React Context (components/providers/auth-context.tsx, workbench-context.tsx, components/chat/ChatProvider.tsx), local state and URL state.
  • Data fetching: Server Components and two Server Actions, plus fetch() to same-origin /api/v1/**; no TanStack Query or SWR. Live updates through Supabase Realtime.
  • Auth client: lib/supabase/client.ts (browser), lib/supabase/server.ts, middleware.ts.

Test IDs strategy

data-testid is the selector contract: 1345 occurrences in 171 files. Kebab-case, prefixed by area, with the entity id appended for rows: login-email, login-signin, billing-overview, failed-renewal-banner, member-row-<id>, ac-row-<id>, run-compare-card-<testId>, settings-nav-<item>. No data-cy. The /qa page warns that login-email appears in both the password and magic-link forms, so scope it.

Database infrastructure

One hosted Supabase Postgres project (its reference is in supabase/migrations/README.md). Region, backups and point-in-time recovery are not in the repo. QA reads it through the read-only qa_inspector_ro role; writes for fixtures use a separate credential referenced by name only.

Monitoring and rollback

No error tracking, uptime monitor or APM: only JSON access logs in Vercel and the health route. Rollback is Vercel-native (promote a previous deployment); a database rollback is a new forward migration.

QA relevance

  • Every suite runs against deployed staging; there is no ephemeral environment.
  • Staging and production share one database: test data is real data next to production rows. Cleanup and workspace scoping are mandatory.
  • Crons never fire on staging: trigger the admin routes by authenticated POST when a test needs them.
  • Recording production URLs in .agents/project.yaml is a pending decision for the team, not done here.

CI/CD

Target repo pipelines

The target has no CI in the committed trees of staging or main (no .github/). A tests workflow (full bun test under the guard, 20-minute timeout) exists only on the unmerged branch chore/test-guard-ci, yet GitHub lists it as active. Quality is enforced by local Git hooks only, which --no-verify bypasses:

HookWhat runs
pre-commitbunx lint-staged (ESLint fix, Prettier), framework gates, and bun run openapi:check when API contract files are staged
pre-pushframework gates (format, lint, env parity, freshness), then the OpenAPI freshness check
commit-msgcommit trailer check
testsbun test is not in any hook

Deployment configuration

ItemFinding
PlatformVercel; deploys on push through the git integration (inferred from a target commit message, not configured in the repo)
vercel.jsoncrons only: GET /api/v1/admin/send-digest at 0 8 * * *, GET /api/v1/admin/storage-cleanup at 0 3 * * *; no build command, regions or headers
Migrationsmanual, through the Supabase MCP apply_migration; no pipeline
Infrastructure as codeNot present (no Terraform, Pulumi, CDK, Docker)

Deployment checklist (inferred, nothing enforces it)

  1. Locally: bun run repo:check and bun test (or bun run test:guarded) pass.
  2. If a route.openapi.ts changed: bun run openapi:gen committed.
  3. Vercel env holds the required names for the target environment.
  4. New migrations applied through apply_migration, then bun run types:gen.
  5. After deploy: curl <env-url>/api/v1/health answers 200 with the right env; /api/openapi loads.
  6. Rollback: promote the previous Vercel deployment.

Exact commands live in each workflow file and in package.json; read them there. Playwright projects: global, UI and API setup, e2e, integration, smoke-ui, smoke-api, teardown.

QA relevance

  • Nothing in the target blocks a merge on failing tests, so the QA nightly regression and smoke runs are the only automated safety net on staging.
  • To validate a changed suite secret before merging, dispatch smoke.yml on the branch: the PR build never logs in.
  • Health and /api/openapi are the cheapest post-deploy probes.

Discovery gaps

Could not be verified from the code; each needs a person, a dashboard or a deeper read.

  • Introspection: count tables through pg_class, not information_schema.tables, which lists only what the read-only role has privileges on (an earlier pass read 46 instead of 52).
  • Branch to environment mapping and deploy trigger (git integration or manual), preview URL pattern, Vercel per-environment env scoping and cron registration status: Vercel dashboard only.
  • Supabase region, backups and point-in-time recovery: Supabase dashboard only. That one project backs every environment comes from the target's release ledger, not from config.
  • Why GitHub lists the tests workflow as active while its file exists only on an unmerged branch: needs gh run list or the dev team.
  • Storage bucket configuration (limits, public flag): the read-only role is denied on the storage schema.
  • pg_cron jobs read from migrations, not from cron.job (denied to the read-only role).
  • .env.example names disagree with lib/env.ts (see backend): worth reporting to the dev team.
  • No latency, availability or scaling targets anywhere; connection pool size unknown.
  • CSRF on cookie-authenticated API writes analysed only as far as SameSite=Lax.
  • Windows of the second rate-limit use (projects/[id]/bugs/heatmap/route.ts) not read.
  • Legacy items not re-verified: URL scheme allowlist, full-text and partial indexes, the one-active-import-per-project index.
  • Exact resolved versions: only declared ranges, except Next.js 15.5.18, React 19.2.6, Tailwind 3.4.19 from the local install (which lacks stripe and resend).
  • The local development recipe was not executed; the session cookie name comes from /qa and the Supabase convention, not from a captured login.
  • Whether Vercel adds HSTS or other headers at the platform level: unknown.
  • A delivery figure for ci-cd was not drawn: the target has no pipeline, so a table says it all.
